title: Transaction Sequencing and Replay Resistance (Monotone Nonce Invariant)

dascp.note: Formalizes the replay-resistance and per-issuer monotone-ordering content of C50-N; the consensus-level GLOBAL ordering aspect of C50-N (cross-validator ordering of unrelated transactions) belongs to BPO:0080 and is intentionally not covered here.

iso20022.note: The property's per-issuer monotone-nonce serves the same uniqueness role at the contract layer that SettlementTransactionIdentification serves in ISO 20022 — a single-use identifier preventing replay and acting as the join key for subsequent status / confirmation messages.

iof.note: Replay-resistance with sufficient cross-context domain separation is the replay-slice of cross-DLT integrity (a relay-evidence or signature accepted on one chain cannot be re-presented on another); the rest of the block — joint-state inventory conservation, wrapped-token lineage, fork-survival of bridge protocols — is carried separately by BPO:0102, and the bridge-relay soundness assumption itself stays out-of-scope as a cryptographic / committee assumption.

descriptions.semantic: Each authorized transaction can be executed at most once and is processed in a sequential position consistent with its issuer's transaction-ordering policy (typically strict-monotone nonce: every accepted transaction from an issuer has nonce equal to the next expected value, which then advances by one). Any attempt to replay a previously-executed transaction, or to execute one with a stale or skipped nonce, is rejected; nonce state advances only when an authorized transaction from the issuer is admitted.
descriptions.system_theoretic: A 1-safety invariant over per-issuer nonce-state monotonicity. The state vocabulary includes `nextNonce(issuer) : Issuer → ℕ` and a per-issuer history. The property asserts that for every accepted tx from issuer i, tx.nonce = nextNonce(i, s_pre), and post-state has nextNonce(i, s_post) = tx.nonce + 1; for every rejected tx, the nonce state is unchanged.
descriptions.security: Replay is one of the canonical authorization failures: a previously-valid authorization is re-presented to obtain its effect a second time. Failure modes — missing nonce check, mis-incremented nonce, accepted out-of-order tx that effectively replays a stale one, missing domain separation that lets a tx authorized for one context be replayed in another — collapse the at-most-once guarantee. The property is the negation of those failure modes.
descriptions.execution_semantics: Realized by including an issuer-keyed nonce in every authorization-bearing transaction (or signed meta-transaction), checking `tx.nonce == nextNonce[issuer]` at the gate, advancing the nonce on success, and reverting on mismatch. For cross-chain or cross-contract usage, domain separation (chain-id, contract-address, function selector) is part of the authorization payload so the same nonce cannot be replayed across contexts. Violations live in: missing nonce check on a privileged or meta-transaction path, advancing the nonce on failure (creating a skip a replay can exploit), missing domain separation, and storage-collision paths that reset the nonce (composes with BPO:0030).
descriptions.formal_verification: A 1-safety property. SMT-checkable as a parametric rule over every accepting path: success implies (pre-nonce == tx.nonce ∧ post-nonce == pre-nonce + 1) AND for every selector, the only path that mutates nextNonce[issuer] is the accepting path of an authorized tx from issuer. The signature-soundness underpinning is delegated to BPO:0074; here we verify the nonce-state discipline above it. Atomic-execution composition with BPO:0020 ensures a reentrant callback cannot re-execute under the same nonce within the same outer call.

formalization.signature: Issuer : Addr; nextNonce : Issuer × State → ℕ; tx = (issuer, nonce, payload, sig, domain); accept : State × Tx → Bool.
formalization.first_order_logic:
Nonce gate:  ∀ s, s', tx . accept(s, tx) ∧ s --[tx]--> s' → tx.nonce = nextNonce(tx.issuer, s) ∧ nextNonce(tx.issuer, s') = nextNonce(tx.issuer, s) + 1.
No-advance-on-reject:  ∀ s, s', tx . ¬accept(s, tx) ∧ s --[tx]--> s' → nextNonce(tx.issuer, s') = nextNonce(tx.issuer, s).
No-out-of-band-write:  every transition that changes nextNonce(i) is an accepting transition of an authorized tx from i.
Domain separation:  ∀ tx . sig.verify(tx) → tx.domain = expectedDomain (chain-id, contract address).

temporal_logic.ltl: G( accept(tx) → tx.nonce = nextNonce(tx.issuer) )   ∧   G( ¬accept(tx) → nextNonce unchanged )   ∧   G( nextNonceChange → accept(tx_for_that_issuer) )

formalization.state_machine: Per-issuer monotone counter automaton: nextNonce(i) advances by exactly 1 on each accepted tx from i, stays put on rejection. The cross-issuer state is the disjoint union of per-issuer counters. The property is monotone strict-monotonicity of each counter under accept-edges only.
formalization.type_theoretic: Each authorization is an affine (single-use) capability keyed by (issuer, nonce, domain). The capability is consumed by acceptance — once consumed, the same (issuer, nonce, domain) triple cannot be re-presented because the issuer's nonce has advanced. Replay becomes a structural type error.
formalization.algebraic: (ℕ, +1) per issuer; nextNonce is a homomorphism from the accepting-tx-sequence to the natural-number successor; replay attempts to invoke a non-successor and is rejected.

relationships.note: Atomicity across external-call boundaries: a reentrant callback cannot re-execute the same nonce-bearing tx within the outer call's window.
The check that tx.issuer is an authorized principal sits on the broader access-control framework; nonce-monotonicity is the per-issuer at-most-once discipline above it.
Signature verification on the nonce-bearing transaction depends on signature-scheme unforgeability.
The nonce storage slot must be isolated from collision rewrites that could reset or overwrite it.

attack_surface.pattern: an authorization-bearing path (meta-tx, permit, signed action) doesn't check or advance a nonce, so the same signed payload is replayable indefinitely
attack_surface.notes: Every signed payload must bind a per-issuer nonce checked at the gate.

attack_surface.pattern: the nonce is advanced before the validity / authorization check, leaving a skipped nonce that a stale-signed tx can later fill or a valid tx can never reach
attack_surface.notes: Advance the nonce only on the success branch.

attack_surface.pattern: a signed payload valid in one chain/contract/function is replayable in another because domain separation is missing or incomplete
attack_surface.notes: EIP-712 domain separator (chain-id, verifyingContract) and per-action type-hash in the signed payload.

attack_surface.pattern: a proxy/delegatecall upgrade or storage-layout drift causes the nonce slot to be overwritten by an unrelated variable, effectively rewinding the nonce
attack_surface.notes: Composes with BPO:0030: isolate the nonce slot.

attack_surface.pattern: an admin path 'rotates' the nonce backwards under the guise of recovery, enabling replay of previously-valid txs
attack_surface.notes: Rotation must move nonce FORWARD only, and require fresh authorization for the new value.

metrics: ratio of accepted vs rejected per issuer (anomaly detection)
invariant_checkpoints: nextNonce(i) is strictly monotone over accepting transitions

strategies.notes: Prove that every method's success path advances nextNonce(issuer) by 1 and that every nextNonce write occurs on such a success path. Trivially SMT-tractable.
Enumerate every selector that consumes a signed payload; confirm each contains the nonce check and the advance.
Identify every storage write to a nonce slot and verify each is on an authorized accepting path.
Stateful handlers that resubmit accepted txs and submit stale-nonce txs; the strict-monotonicity invariant must hold across all random orderings.

testability: replayed tx with same nonce reverts and does not advance nextNonce
cross-chain replay of a signed payload rejected by domain check

runtime: per-issuer nonce check at the authorization gate
EIP-712 domain separator binding chain-id and verifyingContract
static: typed single-use authorization capability per (issuer, nonce, domain)
no proxy-upgrade may relocate the nonce slot
design_patterns: include chain-id and contract address in the signed payload

assumptions.statement: The signature scheme used to authorize nonce-bearing transactions is existentially unforgeable.

Cross-chain and cross-context replay is prevented by sufficient domain separation in the signed payload — chain-id, contract address, function-type-hash. This is the load-bearing wiring detail that the property's correctness rests on outside this contract's scope.

provenance.notes: Authored to formalize the per-issuer monotone-nonce / at-most-once core of DASCP C50-N. The consensus-level global ordering aspect of C50-N (which validator-side mempool/proposer ordering belongs to) is OUT OF SCOPE here and is consensus-property territory (BPO:0080 family).
